import unittest
from stats import StatisticsCalculator

class TestStatisticsCalculator(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.calculator = StatisticsCalculator()
    
    def test_mean_with_positive_numbers(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
        expected = 3.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mean(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_mean_with_negative_numbers(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [-1, -2, -3, -4, -5]
        expected = -3.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mean(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_mean_with_mixed_numbers(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [-2, 0, 2, 4]
        expected = 1.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mean(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_mean_with_empty_list(self):
        # Given
        numbers = []
        
        # When & Then
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.calculator.mean(numbers)
    
    def test_mean_with_single_number(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [42]
        expected = 42.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mean(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_median_odd_count(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [3, 1, 2]
        expected = 2.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.median(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_median_even_count(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4]
        expected = 2.5
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.median(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_median_unsorted_list(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [5, 2, 8, 1, 9]
        expected = 5.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.median(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_median_with_empty_list(self):
        # Given
        numbers = []
        
        # When & Then
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.calculator.median(numbers)
    
    def test_median_with_single_number(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [7]
        expected = 7.0
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.median(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_mode_single_mode(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [1, 2, 2, 3, 4]
        expected = [2]
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mode(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_mode_multiple_modes(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4]
        expected = [1, 2]
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mode(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(sorted(result), sorted(expected))
    
    def test_mode_all_unique(self):
        # Given
        numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
        expected = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mode(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(sorted(result), sorted(expected))
    
    def test_mode_with_empty_list(self):
        # Given
        numbers = []
        
        # When & Then

            self.calculator.mode(numbers)
    
    def test_mode_with_single_number(self):
        # Given

        expected = [5]
        
        # When
        result = self.calculator.mode(numbers)
        
        # Then
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)
    
    def test_mode_with_negative_numbers(self):
